questions.text: Where does the UK Parliament sit?
questions.explanation: The UK is governed by the parliament sitting inWestminster.

questions.text: When did King Edward I of England introduced the Statute of Rhuddlan by which Wales annexed to the Crown of England?
questions.explanation: In 1284King Edward I of England introduced the Statute of Rhuddlan, which annexed Wales to the Crown of England.

questions.text: Which of the following public services can be controlled by the devolved administrations?
questions.explanation: Some public services, such aseducation, are controlled by the devolved administrations.

questions.text: The Senedd has been suspended on a few occasions:
questions.explanation: The Northern Ireland Assemblyhas been suspended on a few occasions.

questions.text: The settlements of Scottish and English Protestants in Ulster (the northern province of Ireland) during the reigns of Elizabeth I and James I, who took over the land from Catholic landholders is known as:
questions.explanation: These settlements were known asplantations.

questions.text: Which of the following jobs is usually unpaid in England, Wales and Scotland?
questions.explanation: In England, Wales and Scotland,Magistrates and Justices of the Peace (JPs)are members of the local community and they usually work unpaid and do not need legal qualifications.

options.text: Magistrates and Justices of the Peace

questions.text: Which of the following is a traditional character of the pantomimes?
questions.explanation: One of the traditional characters of the pantomimes isthe Dame, a woman played by a man.

questions.text: In the UK, most people live in towns and cities and very small parts of Britain are countryside:
questions.explanation: False. Most people live in towns and cities but much of Britain is still countryside.

questions.text: What was the symbol of Lancaster during the Wars of the Roses?
questions.explanation: During the Wars of the Roses, the symbol of Lancaster wasa red rose.

questions.text: After King Alfred the Great defeated the Vikings, many of the Viking invaders stayed in Britain, especially in the east and north of England in an area called:
questions.explanation: Many of the Viking invaders stayed in Britain – especially in the east and north of England in an area known as theDanelaw.

questions.text: The Reform Act of 1832 increased the number of people with the right to vote:
questions.explanation: True. The Reform Act of 1832 had greatly increased the number of people with the right to vote.

questions.text: Which of the following is a famous example of stained glass?

questions.text: Who is the head of the Church of England?
questions.explanation: The monarchis the head of the Church of England.

questions.text: Who is responsible for managing relationships with foreign countries?
questions.explanation: The Foreign Secretaryis responsible for managing relationships with foreign countries.

questions.text: Which TWO of the following poems are from the Middle Ages?
questions.explanation: Poems which survive from the Middle Ages include Chaucer’sCanterbury Tales anda poem calledSir Gawain and the Green Knight, about one of the knights at the court of King Arthur.

questions.text: If a husband forces his wife to have sex, he can be charged with rape:
questions.explanation: True. Any man who forces a woman to have sex, including a woman’s husband, can be charged with rape.

questions.explanation: In 1314 the Scottish, led byRobert the Bruce, defeated the English at the Battle of Bannockburn.

questions.explanation: This statement istrue.

questions.text: How long did the Hundred Years War fought between England and France last for?
questions.explanation: English kings fought a long war with France, called the Hundred Years War (even though it actually lasted116 years).

questions.text: When did Gordon Brown take over as Prime Minister from his predecessor Tony Blair?
questions.explanation: Gordon Brown took over as Prime Minister from Tony Blairin 2007.

questions.explanation: The burial place of one of the Anglo-Saxon kings was atSutton Hoo in modern Suffolk.

questions.explanation: Evelyn Waughwrote satirical novels, including Decline and Fall and Scoop. He is perhaps best known for Brideshead Revisited.
